items.title: 52043_Herman Autrey oral history interview
items.q: I'll call his name, that used to work with me when I was with Charlie Johnson.

ctx.x: He's a -- the one -- the musicians you're talking about now are those who had settled over there, who were living over there.

Yeah, they were living over there. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. I missed seeing the tenor man. I'll call his name, that used to work with me when I was with Charlie Johnson. Heck of a man, too. I called his name the first time. (Unintelligible.)
Oh, Howard Johnson? No, he was an alto.

items.title: 52043_Herman Autrey oral history interview
items.q: I know everybody that was in the band... Bobby -- Bobby Johnson, Tenor saxophone player, yeah... we weren't together, but he had to have been in that band.

ctx.x: Was he -- did he treat the band as if it was a kind of a family thing? Was everybody --

Family, always. Always! That's the way he treated us. And we'd go and record, or go on the stand to play, he'd buy his whiskey, and he'd say well -- okay tell the guy, his valet, bring a bottle for the boys, whatever they're drinking, bring them whatever he's drinking. And should you walk backstage to see him, Hello Fats, how are you? He had a memory like an elephant. Oh, he could remember. Oh, he -- don't think he wouldn't remember you. If you had ever met him and known him. If it was bad or good, he still…

And he say well have a drink. He'll say well I'm very sorry, Fats, very sorry. I only drink Scotch. I don't drink Bourbon. Well, whatever you drink. Well, I like a little Duff-Gordon, a little this -- okay -- a
